title: Maximum Manhattan Distance After K Changes
statement:
A walk starts at `(0, 0)` on an infinite grid and performs the moves of the string `s` one after another: `'N'` adds 1 to y, `'S'` subtracts 1 from y, `'E'` adds 1 to x and `'W'` subtracts 1 from x. Before the walk you may rewrite at most `k` characters of `s`, each to any of the four letters.

Return the largest Manhattan distance from the origin, `|x| + |y|`, that the walk can reach at any moment, over all ways of choosing the rewrites.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every way to rewrite at most `k` letters is exponential. Instead, look at one moment: after the first `i + 1` moves the walk stands at `(x, y)`. Some of those moves cancel others (an `S` against an `N`, a `W` against an `E`). Rewriting one cancelling move to point the other way turns a step back into a step forward, so the distance grows by exactly 2, and no single rewrite can do better. With `k` rewrites the distance grows by `2k`, but it can never exceed `i + 1`, the number of moves made. So the best distance at that moment is `min(|x| + |y| + 2k, i + 1)`, and the answer is the largest such value over all moments.

## Approach

1. Track the position `(x, y)` of the original walk and the answer `best`.
2. For each index `i`, apply the move `s[i]`.
3. Compute `distance = |x| + |y|` after the first `i + 1` moves.
4. Spending the rewrites on cancelling moves adds `2k`, capped at `i + 1`: that is `reachable`.
5. Keep the largest `reachable` in `best` and return it.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "NWSE"`, `k = 1`, so each moment can gain up to 2.

| i | move | (x, y) | distance | reachable |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | N | (0, 1) | 1 | min(3, 1) = 1 |
| 1 | W | (-1, 1) | 2 | min(4, 2) = 2 |
| 2 | S | (-1, 0) | 1 | min(3, 3) = 3 |
| 3 | E | (0, 0) | 0 | min(2, 4) = 2 |

The answer is 3, reached at `i = 2` by rewriting the `S` to `N`, which puts the walk at `(-1, 2)`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), one pass over `s`.
- Space: O(1), a few counters.

## Pitfalls

- The farthest point can come midway: the walk may end closer to the origin than it was earlier, so check every prefix, not only the end.
- Cap at `i + 1`: with a large `k` the distance still cannot exceed the number of moves made.
- A rewrite gains 2, not 1: it removes a step back and adds a step forward.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `x`, `y` | position after the moves so far, without rewrites |
| `i` | index of the current move |
| `distance` | Manhattan distance of `(x, y)` from the origin |
| `reachable` | best distance at this moment using up to `k` rewrites |
| `best` | largest `reachable` so far |

narration.2: x is the east-west coordinate of the walk as written.
narration.4: best holds the largest distance found at any moment so far.
narration.6: Process the moves in order; after move i the walk has made i + 1 moves.
narration.7: Read the move and update the matching coordinate.
narration.8: N moves one step north, raising y.
narration.10: S moves one step south, lowering y.
narration.12: E moves one step east, raising x.
narration.14: Otherwise the move is W, one step west, lowering x.
narration.16: How far the unchanged walk is from the origin right now.
narration.17: Each rewrite of a cancelling move adds 2, but the distance cannot exceed the i + 1 moves made.
narration.18: Keep the best moment seen so far.
narration.20: The largest distance over all moments is the answer.
